podcast.title: Harper Valley PTA - Movie and TV Show
podcast.body: The hit song "Harper Valley PTA" inspired a movie starring Barbara Eden, known from "I Dream of Jeannie." In 1980, it was further adapted into a TV show. "Harper Valley PTA also inspired a movie starring Barbara Eden... and then in 1980 it became a TV show."

srcs.episode: Ep. 23 - Women of Country Music in the 70s

podcast.title: Image vs. Authenticity Struggle
podcast.body: Despite singing a song about a strong woman, Genie C. Riley faced a cruel irony where her producer, Shelby Singleton, heavily controlled her image. Singleton transformed her into an "over-sexed hillbilly girl" trope, making her wear mini skirts on stage and even shortening a floor-length gown she intended to wear to the 1968 Country Music Association Awards. This exploitation extended to promotional appearances where her husband was forbidden from accompanying her when he tried to intervene. "It is this cruel irony that she was singing a song about a strong woman but she was not permitted her own authenticity."

srcs.episode: Ep. 23 - Women of Country Music in the 70s

podcast.title: Transformation to Gospel Singer
podcast.body: After years of struggling for control over her image and career, Genie C. Riley broke her contract with Shelby Singleton's Plantation label and moved to MGM. By the end of the 1970s, she had become a gospel singer, performing in full-length gowns, an image she presumably controlled herself. "Eventually, Riley broke her contract with Singleton and went to MGM to try to assert some control over her own career and her life and by the end of the decade she was a gospel singer who performed in these full-length gowns and presumably was now the person who had taken some control of her image."
